Anybody played Sublevel Zero? Good, Bad. Any thoughts?

Yes, I have it. My opinion is based on the fact that I loved Descent back in the day.

As a game that used Descent as its inspiration it does a great job at making it feel close to what Descent did. Graphics and sounds remind me of those old games. While the levels are randomly generated, there are enough templates to make it very unique. Two problems I have with the maps are that some of the caves are very easy to get disoriented and that there should have been more elaborate maps, they are mostly pretty linear. Some forks in the road but not many, usually 1, rarely 2. Difficulty really ramps up by the 3rd level. But, will get easier with each play through, once you get familiar with the items and what they can craft into.

The question isn't if it's a good game, but more so "is the game right for you?" If you are someone who loved Descent and similar 6 degrees of movement games, if you don't care about a story and just want to blow shit up, you don't have a problem with things like permadeath and randomly generated levels, and you like the retro feel, then I say it's a no brainer.

EDIT: I felt like I should have included this...

There does not seem to be a steady stream of updates, but unless they are going to add more templates or items, I don't see a reason for updates. The game was made using Unity and with that, they support Windows, OSX, and Linux. My experience has been with the Linux build and has been a great experience. I have not tried it with a controller, only a keyboard and mouse. One small problem is that the mouse sensitivity seems to be really slow, even when cranked all the way up. This is not unique to Linux because Totalbiscuit had the same complaint in his WTF video and he's on Windows. But, once you get used to the speed of the mouse it becomes like second nature.

I like it, but 6dof shooters aren't for everyone. It is easy to get disoriented in some rooms, and the 3D map is kind of tough to navigate.

Other than that, I enjoy it a lot.

Yeah, this is a great Descent clone roguelike. The graphics are simple, but stylized and don't look bad, but that also means it runs good on pretty much anything.

Plus, it has VR support, which is really neat for a game like this. If you have or are planning to get an Oculus Rift or Vive, this is a must have game.

Even if you don't, it's worth the price. It's just a fun title to fly around and it's never the same twice.
